intent: Let trace_shell_split.sh shadow additional binaries per run, so scripts that clone from AUR or build packages can be traced without touching the network or the package set.
scope: Non-goal: git/curl/wget/makepkg are deliberately not added to the default set
changes: Rename STUBBED_COMMANDS to DEFAULT_STUBBED_COMMANDS and add a --stub a,b,c flag whose names are shadowed for that run only.
Document why git and friends stay out of the default set: many scripts read git state harmlessly, so a blanket stub would change what they observe rather than protect anything.

verification.command: trace_shell_split.sh on a fixture calling `git clone` and `curl`, with --stub git,curl,makepkg
verification.evidence: Trace captured 'git clone https://example.com/repo.git' and 'curl -sL https://example.com/x'; stdout reached 'reached the end'. No repository was cloned and no request left the machine.
Still exit status 1 with an empty trace and no stdout -- the --stub change did not weaken detection.
Still four 'circular name reference' warnings captured in stderr.

risks: A caller who forgets --stub for a script that shells out to git or curl gets a real clone or a real request. The header comment tells the reader to grep for network and build verbs first; that remains a human step.
IFS-splitting the --stub value means a binary name containing a comma cannot be passed, which no real binary does.
rollback: Revert the commit; the harness returns to a fixed default stub list.
Re-run the three fixtures and confirm the same exit statuses.
